answer: Each identity claims one peat-bog plot, locks an 80-credit bond, and plants a yarrow marker at its nadir point. Each epoch it files the water-table depth from a prism staff, keyed to that serial. An auditor re-levels the stake and recomputes the depth from the public water-table table; over 3 percent off, a missing marker, or one serial on two plots burns it. First plot 44, kth 44+5(k-1), 1000th 5039, so 1000 fakes pay 2,541,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-stake ring fails: one staff serial cannot level two plots at once. An honest keeper pays 44 once, bond back after audit.
